applicability_conditions: Developed for the low-density Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C steel during the multi-axial forging (MAF) process; implemented into a 3-D finite element model via an ABAQUS VUMAT subroutine using six state-dependent variables (SDVs).
latex: \sigma_{flow} = \left(\sigma_{0} + k(d_{f}^{-1/2} - d_{0}^{-1/2}) + \alpha M G b((\rho_{f}^{1/2} - \rho_{0}^{1/2}) + B\varepsilon^{n}\right)\left[1 + C\ln\left(\frac{\dot{\varepsilon}}{\dot{\varepsilon}_{0}}\right)\right]\left[1 - \left(\frac{T - T_{r}}{T_{m} - T_{r}}\right)^{m}\right]
purpose: Modified Johnson–Cook constitutive model that expresses the flow stress of the material as a function of grain-size refinement (Hall–Petch type term) and dislocation-density strengthening during multi-axial forging (MAF), combined with strain-hardening, strain-rate and thermal-softening terms.

symbols.meaning: Flow stress of the material (predicted by the modified J–C model)
Initial/base flow stress (original J–C yield term)
Strain hardening coefficient of the J–C model
Strain hardening exponent of the J–C model
Strain rate sensitivity coefficient of the J–C model
Thermal softening exponent of the J–C model

unmapped: The modified J–C model (Eq. 6) integrates the influence of the strain-dependent dislocation density (Eq. 7) and the grain size (Eq. 8) parameters, both of which contribute to the yield strength after each MAF pass.
The original J–C model parameters of the current material have been evaluated in the authors' previous study [26]; material properties are summarized in Table 4.
